literal: Liu Gui, acting for Fen Province, abandoned the city and came to surrender.
idiomatic: Liu Gui, who was administering Fen Province, abandoned his post and surrendered.

literal: In the intercalary third month, Erzhu Tianguang from Chang'an, Zhao from Bing Province, Dulü from Luoyang, and Zhongyuan from Dong Commandery all assembled at Ye; the host was said to number two hundred thousand. They camped along the Huan River. Emperor Jiemin put Changsun Chengye in charge as Grand Chief of the Eastern Headquarters.
idiomatic: In the intercalary third month Erzhu Tianguang marched from Chang'an, Zhao from Bing Province, Dulü from Luoyang, and Zhongyuan from Dong Commandery to meet at Ye with a force said to number two hundred thousand. They camped along the Huan River while Emperor Jiemin put Changsun Chengye in overall command as Grand Eastern Chief.

literal: Shenwu ordered Feng Longzhi to hold Ye and marched out himself to encamp at Zimo.
idiomatic: Gao Huan left Feng Longzhi to hold Ye and marched out to encamp at Zimo.

literal: At the time cavalry did not reach two thousand and infantry not thirty thousand — the many and the few could not match.
idiomatic: He had fewer than two thousand horse and not thirty thousand foot—the odds were impossible.

literal: Thereupon at Hanling he formed a circular array, linking oxen and donkeys to block the return road; the officers and troops all had the will to die, and struck them from four sides.
idiomatic: At Hanling he formed a ring formation and chained oxen and donkeys to block retreat. Officers and men alike resolved to die, then struck from every side.

literal: Erzhu Zhao blamed Shenwu for turning against him. Shenwu said: "We joined forces to support the royal house — where is the emperor now?
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao accused Gao Huan of betrayal. Gao Huan said, "We joined forces to serve the throne—where is the emperor now?

literal: " Zhao said: "Yong'an wrongly killed the Heavenly Pillar; I am only avenging him.
idiomatic: Zhao said, "Emperor Yong'an wrongly killed the Heavenly Pillar. I am only avenging him.

literal: " Shenwu said: "I personally heard the Heavenly Pillar's plan in former days — you stood before the gate. How can you say you did not mean to rebel?
idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "I heard the Heavenly Pillar's plan myself—you stood at the gate. Can you say you never meant to rebel?

literal: Moreover, when a lord kills his minister, what vengeance is owed?
idiomatic: When a lord kills his minister, what vengeance is owed?

literal: Today righteousness is severed.
idiomatic: Today our bond of righteousness is broken.

literal: " Thereupon they joined battle and routed him utterly.
idiomatic: They joined battle and routed him utterly.

literal: Erzhu Zhao clutched his chest before Murong Shaozong and said: "Had I heeded you, it would not have come to this!
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao clutched his chest before Murong Shaozong and cried, "Had I listened to you, this would never have happened!

literal: " He was about to flee lightly.
idiomatic: He was about to flee with a light escort.

literal: Shaozong turned the banners and sounded the horns, gathered the scattered troops, restored military order, and marched west.
idiomatic: Shaozong reversed the banners and sounded the horns, rallied the scattered troops, restored order, and marched west.

literal: Gao Jishi pursued the rout with seven horsemen, crossed Yema Ridge, and met Zhao.
idiomatic: Gao Jishi pursued with seven riders, crossed Yema Ridge, and met Zhao.

literal: Gao Ao looked and did not see him; he wept and said: "I have lost my brother!
idiomatic: Gao Ao looked and could not see him; he wept and said, "I have lost my brother!

literal: " Late at night Jishi returned, his sleeves drenched in blood.
idiomatic: Late that night Jishi returned, his sleeves drenched in blood.

literal: Husi Chun raced by forced marches and seized the River Bridge first.
idiomatic: Husi Chun raced ahead by forced marches and seized the River Bridge first.

literal: Initially, in the tenth month of the first year of Putai, Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and Venus gathered at Zi and Shen — their light was very bright.
idiomatic: Earlier, in the tenth month of Wei Putai 1 (531), Jupiter, Mars, Saturn, and Venus gathered at Zi and Shen, shining with unusual brilliance.

literal: The court astronomers divined that a true king would rise.
idiomatic: The court astronomers divined that a true king would rise.

literal: At that time Shenwu had risen at Xindu; by now he had broken Zhao and the rest.
idiomatic: Gao Huan had risen at Xindu—and by now he had broken Zhao and the rest.

literal: In the fourth month Husi Chun seized Tianguang and Dulü and sent them to Luoyang.
idiomatic: In the fourth month Husi Chun seized Tianguang and Dulü and sent them to Luoyang.

literal: Changsun Chengye sent commanders Jia Xianzhi and Zhang Huan into Luoyang to seize Shilong and Yanbo and behead them.
idiomatic: Changsun Chengye sent commanders Jia Xianzhi and Zhang Huan into Luoyang to seize Shilong and Yanbo and behead them.

literal: Zhao fled to Bing Province.
idiomatic: Zhao fled to Bing Province.

literal: Zhongyuan fled to Liang Province and there died.
idiomatic: Zhongyuan fled to Liang Province and died there.

literal: At that time, with the wicked eliminated, the court rejoiced.
idiomatic: With the wicked eliminated, the court rejoiced.

literal: Initially, in the month before the battle, Zhang Shao of Zhangwu was suddenly seized at night by several horsemen who carried him over the wall to a great general. He was ordered to guide the army toward Ye, it being said that one who had received Heaven's mandate would aid in destroying the wicked.
idiomatic: Before the battle, in the month prior, Zhang Shao of Zhangwu was seized at night by several horsemen who carried him over the wall to a great general. He was ordered to guide the army toward Ye for one who had received Heaven's mandate to destroy the wicked.

literal: Shao looked back — the troops could not be counted; they marched in perfect order without a sound.
idiomatic: Shao looked back—the host was beyond counting, marching in perfect silence.

literal: When they were about to reach Ye, they released him.
idiomatic: Nearing Ye, they released him.

literal: On the day of battle the Erzhu soldiers saw horsemen closing in from every side of the formation — Heaven's aid, it was said.
idiomatic: On the day of battle Erzhu soldiers saw horsemen closing in from every side of the field—Heaven's aid, men said.

literal: Soon Shenwu reached Luoyang, deposed Emperor Jiemin and the Zhongxing ruler, and enthroned Emperor Xiaowu.
idiomatic: Soon Gao Huan reached Luoyang, deposed Emperor Jiemin and the Zhongxing emperor, and enthroned Emperor Xiaowu.

literal: Once Xiaowu had taken the throne, he appointed Shenwu Grand Chancellor, Pillar-of-State Grand General, Grand Preceptor, and hereditary governor of Ding Province, raising his fief together with previous grants to one hundred fifty thousand households.
idiomatic: Once enthroned, Emperor Xiaowu made Gao Huan Grand Chancellor, Pillar-of-State Grand General, Grand Preceptor, and hereditary governor of Ding Province, raising his fief to one hundred fifty thousand households in all.

literal: Shenwu declined the Pillar-of-State title and surrendered fifty thousand households.
idiomatic: Gao Huan declined the Pillar-of-State title and surrendered fifty thousand households.

literal: On the renchen day he returned to Ye; the Wei emperor saw him off at Ganfu Mountain, clasping hands in farewell.
idiomatic: On the renchen day he returned to Ye; the Wei emperor saw him off at Ganfu Mountain, clasping hands in parting.

literal: On the renyin day of the seventh month Shenwu led his army north to campaign against Erzhu Zhao.
idiomatic: On the renyin day of the seventh month Gao Huan led his army north against Erzhu Zhao.

literal: Feng Longzhi said: "Palace Attendants Husi Chun, Helü Sheng, and Jia Xianzhi once served the Erzhu — all turned and bit their masters. Now in the capital, favored and trusted, they will surely sow the seeds of disaster.
idiomatic: Feng Longzhi said, "Palace Attendants Husi Chun, Helü Sheng, and Jia Xianzhi once served the Erzhu and all turned on their masters. Now favored in the capital, they will surely sow discord.

literal: " Shenwu took this deeply to heart and sent Tianguang and Dulü back to the capital to be executed.
idiomatic: Gao Huan took this to heart and sent Tianguang and Dulü back to the capital to be executed.

literal: He thereupon entered by Fekou Pass.
idiomatic: He then entered through Fekou Pass.

literal: Erzhu Zhao plundered Jinyang heavily and retreated north to hold Xiurong.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao plundered Jinyang and retreated north to hold Xiurong.

literal: Bing Province was pacified.
idiomatic: Bing Province was pacified.

literal: Shenwu, because Jinyang was blocked on four sides, built the Grand Chancellor's headquarters there and settled.
idiomatic: Because Jinyang was walled in on four sides, Gao Huan built his Grand Chancellor's headquarters there and made it his base.

literal: Once Erzhu Zhao had reached Xiurong, he split his forces to hold the passes and raided in and out.
idiomatic: At Xiurong Zhao split his forces to hold the passes and raided back and forth.

literal: Shenwu loudly proclaimed he would attack; his army marched out only to halt — four times this happened — and Zhao grew slack.
idiomatic: Gao Huan loudly proclaimed he would attack, yet his army marched out and halted four times, until Zhao grew careless.

literal: Shenwu guessed that at the New Year Zhao would be feasting; he sent Dou Tai with elite cavalry at a gallop — three hundred li in one day and one night — and followed with the main army.
idiomatic: Guessing Zhao would be feasting at the New Year, Gao Huan sent Dou Tai with elite cavalry at a gallop—three hundred li in a day and a night—and followed with the main army.

literal: In the first month of the second year Dou Tai suddenly arrived at Erzhu Zhao's headquarters.
idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Dou Tai suddenly arrived at Erzhu Zhao's headquarters.

literal: The troops, drunk and idle from feasting, suddenly saw Dou Tai's army and fled in panic.
idiomatic: The troops were drunk and idle from feasting; seeing Dou Tai's army they fled in panic.

literal: He pursued and broke them at Chihong Ridge.
idiomatic: He pursued and broke them at Chihong Ridge.

literal: Zhao hanged himself; Shenwu came in person and gave him a lavish burial.
idiomatic: Zhao hanged himself; Gao Huan came in person and gave him a lavish burial.

literal: Murong Shaozong held Wutu City with Erzhu Rong's wife and children and the remaining troops; he surrendered, and for old righteousness's sake Shenwu treated him with great generosity.
idiomatic: Murong Shaozong held Wutu City with Erzhu Rong's family and the remnants; he surrendered, and for old righteousness's sake Gao Huan treated him with great generosity.

literal: When Shenwu entered Luoyang, commanders Qiao Ning and Zhang Ziqi of Erzhu Zhongyuan's force submitted from Huatai. Shenwu beheaded them both for aiding rebellion and for repeated treachery.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan entered Luoyang, commanders Qiao Ning and Zhang Ziqi of Erzhu Zhongyuan's force submitted from Huatai. Gao Huan beheaded them for aiding rebellion and for repeated treachery.

literal: Husi Chun was inwardly ill at ease from this; with Prince Nanyang Baoqu and Military Guard Generals Yuan Pi, Wei Guang, and Wang Sizheng he slandered Shenwu to the Wei emperor.
idiomatic: Husi Chun was inwardly ill at ease; with Prince Nanyang Baoqu and Military Guard Generals Yuan Pi, Wei Guang, and Wang Sizheng he slandered Gao Huan to the Wei emperor.

literal: Palace Attendant Yuan Shibi also memorialized that Shenwu had showed great disrespect in receiving the emperor's edicts.
idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yuan Shibi also memorialized that Gao Huan had shown great disrespect in receiving imperial edicts.

literal: Thus the Wei emperor turned his heart toward Helü Yue.
idiomatic: Thus the Wei emperor turned his heart toward Helü Yue.

literal: Initially, in Emperor Xiaoming's day, Luoyang folk struck two daggers against each other, and a song ran: "Bronze dagger strikes iron dagger — the Yuan clan's great generals will end.
idiomatic: Earlier, in Emperor Xiaoming's day, Luoyang folk struck two daggers together, and a song ran: "Bronze dagger strikes iron dagger—the Yuan clan's great generals will end.

literal: " The curious took the two daggers to mean Tuoba and Helü — both clans, they said, were doomed to fall.
idiomatic: The curious took the two daggers to mean Tuoba and Helü—both clans, they said, were doomed to fall.

literal: At that time Minister of Works Gao Qian secretly warned Shenwu that the emperor was divided in heart; Shenwu sealed the letter and forwarded it.
idiomatic: Minister of Works Gao Qian secretly warned Gao Huan that the emperor's heart was divided; Gao Huan sealed the letter and forwarded it.

literal: The Wei emperor had him killed and secretly ordered East Xuzhou governor Pan Shaoye to tell Changle governor Pang Cangying to kill his younger brother Ao.
idiomatic: The Wei emperor had him killed and secretly ordered East Xuzhou governor Pan Shaoye to tell Changle governor Pang Cangying to kill his younger brother Gao Ao.

literal: Ao had already heard of his brother's death; he drove his spear into a pillar, set strong men to seize Shaoye on the road, found the secret edict in his robe collar, and fled to submit.
idiomatic: Ao had already heard of his brother's death. He drove his spear into a pillar, set strong men to seize Shaoye on the road, found the secret edict in his robe collar, and fled to Gao Huan.

literal: Shenwu clasped his head and wept, saying: "The Son of Heaven wrongly killed the Minister of Works!
idiomatic: Gao Huan clasped his head and wept, saying, "The Son of Heaven wrongly killed the Minister of Works!

literal: " He at once sent the white martial banner to condole with his family.
idiomatic: He at once sent the white martial banner to condole with his family.

literal: At that time Gao Qian's next-youngest brother Shen was in Guang Province, governing with harsh severity and also taking bribes from his subordinates; the Wei emperor sent someone to replace him.
idiomatic: Gao Qian's next-youngest brother Shen was in Guang Province, governing with harsh severity and taking bribes from his subordinates; the Wei emperor sent someone to replace him.

literal: Shen heard of the trouble and was about to flee to Liang.
idiomatic: Shen heard of the trouble and was about to flee to Liang.

literal: His followers said: "Your family's merit is great — they will surely not punish brothers together.
idiomatic: His followers said, "Your family's merit is great—they will surely not punish brothers together.

literal: " He put on shabby clothes, pushed a deer cart, and returned to Bohai.
idiomatic: He put on shabby clothes, pushed a deer cart, and returned to Bohai.

literal: He met the imperial envoy on the road and also fled to submit.
idiomatic: He met the imperial envoy on the road and fled to Gao Huan as well.

literal: Thereupon the breach between the Wei emperor and Shenwu was complete.
idiomatic: The breach between the Wei emperor and Gao Huan was now complete.

literal: The Azhiluo barbarians had regularly paid tribute before Zhengguang; once the Wei court fell into turmoil, they all rebelled.
idiomatic: The Azhiluo barbarians had regularly paid tribute before Zhengguang; once the Wei court fell into turmoil, they all rebelled.

literal: Shenwu sent envoys to summon them and they at once submitted.
idiomatic: Gao Huan sent envoys to summon them and they at once submitted.

literal: Earlier an edict had dissolved the Eastern Headquarters because the rebels were pacified.
idiomatic: Earlier an edict had dissolved the Eastern Headquarters because the rebels were pacified.

literal: Now, because distant peoples had submitted, Shenwu was again given the Grand Eastern Headquarters with discretion to act as needed.
idiomatic: Now, because distant peoples had submitted, Gao Huan was again given the Grand Eastern Headquarters with discretion to act as needed.

literal: Shenwu regularly bestowed grain and cloth on them; advisers called it wasted expense, but Shenwu would not listen and continued to comfort them as before.
idiomatic: Gao Huan regularly bestowed grain and cloth on them; advisers called it wasted expense, but he would not listen and continued to comfort them as before.

literal: Their chieftains such as Tuchen were grateful and obeyed every order — rescuing Cao Ni and taking Moqi Shouluogan — and proved of great use.
idiomatic: Their chieftains such as Tuchen were grateful and obeyed every order—rescuing Cao Ni and taking Moqi Shouluogan—proving of great use.

literal: The Feiyetou barbarian of Hexi, Qidouling Yili, held Hechi, relying on the terrain and a great following; Shenwu's chief secretary Hou Jing repeatedly summoned him but he would not submit.
idiomatic: The Feiyetou barbarian of Hexi, Qidouling Yili, held Hechi behind strong terrain with a great following; Gao Huan's chief secretary Hou Jing repeatedly summoned him, but he would not submit.

literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972, as the base for collation.
idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
